requirements.statement: A feature cannot close (by /audit-build or /close-feature) while any failure waived under `Blocking: must-pass only` has no defect issue in the project's tracker. The close files each missing one, labelled `defect`, records its URL on the ledger row, and refuses to close, naming the rows, when one cannot be filed. Must pass: yes.
requirements.source: TRD docs/TRD/every-waived-failure-filed-as-a-defect-issue.md, Objectives table, row O1 (plus Intended Change item 1, Close gate)

requirements.statement: When the project declares no reachable tracker in stack.md `## Issue Tracker`, `Blocking: must-pass only` waives nothing: verification runs as `all criteria`, and the verification report says why. Must pass: yes.
requirements.source: TRD, Objectives table, row O2 (plus Intended Change item 2, No tracker, no waiver)

requirements.statement: A waived failure is filed at most once: file-followups, a resumed run and a fix round never file or re-record a row whose issue URL is already recorded. Must pass: yes.
requirements.source: TRD, Objectives table, row O3 (plus Intended Change item 3, Never twice)

requirements.statement: No step of the framework closes a waived-failure defect issue; only a person does. Must pass: no.
requirements.source: TRD, Objectives table, row O4 (plus Intended Change item 4, Never closed by a step)

requirements.statement: The owner-facing text (verification.md section 5c template, /verification-setup, docs/reference/, and the TRD-authoring guidance on the `Must pass` column) says a waived failure is filed as a defect issue. Must pass: no.

Close gate: before writing closed.json, /audit-build (close step) and /close-feature run `node .claude/lib/waived-defects.js gate`. It reads the ledger first and checks the tracker only when an unfiled waived row exists. A waived row is a criterion whose latest row over all rows is a [non-blocking] row. For each unfiled one it files one labelled `defect` issue, prints { ok, filed, already, failed }, and on ok:false writes no close record, opens no PR, and ends COMMAND STUCK naming each row. Serves: no task claims it directly; closest are FIX-001 and FIX-004.

No tracker, no waiver: read-blocking-policy takes --stack; when declared policy is must-pass and the tracker is absent, none, unparseable, or GitHub-unreachable, it returns policy 'all' with declared 'must-pass' and a waiverRefused reason. The workflow carries blockingNote into every report, and renderReport emits one **Blocking**: line gated on its presence. Serves: no task claims it directly; closest are FIX-002 and FIX-003.

Never twice: recordNonBlockingFollowups treats a [non-blocking] row whose issue is already filed as recorded (reads resolved rows too); file-followups files a [non-blocking] row only through waived-defects.js gate, which skips rows with a recorded URL. Serves: no task claims it directly; closest are FIX-002 and FIX-005.

Never closed by a step: waived-defects.js runs only issue create, label list, label create and repo view (a test records every call); the close-issue contract gains one sentence saying a waived-defect issue is closed only by a later feature that cites it. Serves: no task claims it directly; closest are FIX-001 and FIX-005.
Readout: filed waived rows drop out of the DISCOVERED summary, so both close commands list each filed issue's URL with its criterion in STATE. Serves: no task claims it directly; closest is FIX-004.

Each gh call uses spawnSync with array arguments, never a shell string; the issue body goes through --body-file, never inline --body. Source: TRD Task Grounding FIX-001 'Follow' (CLAUDE.md command-injection rule). Serves: no task claims it as a requirement; it is an implementation constraint of FIX-001.

Never run gh issue create to probe whether the tracker works; reachability is checked with gh repo view only. Source: TRD Task Grounding FIX-001 Careful and Decision section. Serves: implementation constraint of FIX-001.
requirements.source: TRD, Task Grounding, FIX-001 Careful; Decision

requirements.statement: Circular requires between waived-defects.js and functional-verification.js are lazy (inside the function or CLI branch that needs them), never top-level. Source: TRD Decision. Serves: implementation constraint of FIX-001 and FIX-002.
The .claude/ mirrors of every touched packages/core file are byte-identical to their packages/core source. Source: TRD FIX-004 and FIX-006 acceptance criteria. Serves: FIX-004, FIX-006.
requirements.source: TRD, Master Task List acceptance criteria for FIX-004 and FIX-006

tasks.description: New library waived-defects.js: parse ## Issue Tracker, check reachability, list waived rows with recorded URL, build and file defect issues, record URLs; CLI subcommands tracker, gate, record-filed. Serves O1, O3, O4. Acceptance: npx jest packages/core/lib/waived-defects.test.js passes with cases (a)-(j) as listed in the TRD (file once and not twice; failure refuses with no filed marker; Tracker none with waived row refuses; recorded URL goes to already; runner limited to four commands; Tracker none with no waived rows is ok and never calls runner; met row retires a waived row; second row reuses URL; marker-write failure carries URL; record-filed read back by gate).

functional-verification.js: recordNonBlockingFollowups skips a ref whose latest [non-blocking] row is filed; read-blocking-policy takes --stack and refuses the waiver with no reachable tracker; renderReport renders a **Blocking**: line from input.blockingNote; the Not blocking line says filed as defect issues. Serves O2, O3. Acceptance: npx jest packages/core/lib/functional-verification.test.js passes with new cases; output unchanged without --stack; report byte-identical without blockingNote except the Not blocking wording.

implement-trd section 8.1a and verify-build pass --stack to read-blocking-policy and blockingNote (from waiverRefused) to the workflow; verify-functional.js validates blockingNote and carries it into every report input; DECISIONS says the waiver was refused; readout wording says filed as defect issues. Serves O2. Acceptance: npx jest on verify-command-surface.test.js and verify-functional.test.js passes with POLICY_CMD and field-list assertions updated and new blockingNote cases.

audit-build close step and close-feature close step run waived-defects.js gate (--closed-by audit / owner) before writing closed.json; on ok:false write no close record, open no PR, still write records ref, end COMMAND STUCK naming each row with Next:; Linear/Jira rows filed via their skill then record-filed then gate re-run; STATE lists each filed URL; close-feature framing gains the exception. Serves O1. Acceptance: new packages/core/commands/waived-defects-close-prose.test.js passes (gate before closed.json write; refusal text names no close record, records-ref write, record-filed, and never /close-feature as next step for audit-build; no ship.md step needed; .claude mirrors byte-identical).

file-followups files a [non-blocking] row only through waived-defects.js gate and never refiles a row with a recorded URL; close-issue contract gains the sentence that a waived-defect issue is never closed by the feature that waived it. Serves O3, O4. Acceptance: npx jest packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js packages/core/contracts/ship-tracker.test.js passes with both sentences asserted.

Owner-facing text: verification.md section 5c template (both copies), verification-setup SKILL.md question sentence, docs/reference/verification.md, contracts/functional-verification.md, and the Must pass guidance in plan.md, create-trd.md, trd-authoring.md say a waived failure is filed as a defect issue and must-pass only needs a declared tracker. Serves O5. Acceptance: npx jest on verification-setup skill-md.test.js and packages/core/commands passes; grep finds no listed-and-filed-as wording; .claude mirrors byte-identical.

[LIVE] Headless fixture run: scaffolded fixture slot with Blocking: must-pass only, a Issue Tracker naming a GitHub project, a stub gh on PATH logging calls, and a ledger with one [non-blocking] row; run /close-feature headless and capture that the issue was filed before closed.json was written. Second run on a fresh feature with gh issue create set to fail must show no closed.json and a STUCK banner. Evidence under .trd-state/every-waived-failure-filed-as-a-defect-issue/evidence/live/. Serves O1.

open_questions: OQ-1: Is creating the `defect` label in the project's repo, when missing, acceptable as part of the owner-authorized filing? Assumed: yes, recorded as an OWNER-CALL. Owner-only: yes.
could_not_verify: Reachability for Linear and Jira is assumed from the declaration alone; a declared but unreachable Linear/Jira tracker is caught only when the close tries to file, which then refuses to close (the safe direction).
A real GitHub issue is not filed in any test: the fixture uses a stub gh. The gh issue create / gh label argument shapes are checked against gh --help, not against a live repo.
